name: Sankey Studio
summary: Turn a spreadsheet into charts Excel can't draw: Sankey diagrams for things moving through stages, and chord diagrams for exchanges that go both ways. Import from Excel, export a crisp image. Everything runs in your browser.
steps: Open the tool and drop in an Excel file, or try one of the samples first.
Pick the chart in the side panel. The app works out which columns to use, and you can change them.
Leave rows out with the filters, set colours and number format, and save the view back into your workbook.
Copy the image straight into a slide, or download it as SVG or PNG.

charts.name: Sankey
charts.line: Where things go, step by step.
charts.analogy: Like a river splitting into streams: the wider a stream, the more went that way.
charts.useWhen: You want to see how orders, money or people move through stages, and where they drop out.
charts.youGet: Every path from start to finish in one picture, with the total at each step.
charts.sheet: One row per item with a column per stage (Channel, Status, Outcome), or From, To and Value columns.

charts.name: Chord
charts.line: Who exchanges with whom, both ways.
charts.analogy: Like a map of trade between countries: each country is a slice of the ring, and the bands are what goes back and forth.
charts.useWhen: Things flow both ways between the same parties, such as charges between departments or staff moving between teams. A Sankey can't draw that.
charts.youGet: Who gives, who takes, which pairs trade most, and whether each exchange balances. Or, for items in the same order, which ones go together.
charts.sheet: From and To columns with an amount, or an order number and an item on each row.
